transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because things at work have been… tense, and I’m probably not explaining it perfectly. After I got this county safety award, some people started looking at my inspection reports in a way that feels off—like twisting what I wrote, asking these pointed budget questions, almost like they’re trying to make me look crooked.

My supervisor says it’s just normal review, and maybe that’s what he has to say, but I can tell there’s something coordinated going on to discredit me. I don’t want to sound dramatic, but it’s been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
Do you think these people at work are specifically targeting you?

I mean… yes, I think so, though I don’t want to sound paranoid or like I’m blaming everybody. It’s more certain people, after that safety award. The way they’ve been going over my reports and asking these budget questions feels pointed, like they’re trying to twist things so I look dishonest. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, and maybe I’m not saying it right, but it really does feel coordinated to discredit me.
Do you think there's any possibility that your coworkers' actions could be explained by something other than a coordinated effort to discredit you?

I mean… I guess there’s always some possibility, right? I don’t want to be difficult or act like I know everyone’s motives for sure.

But honestly, it doesn’t feel like just normal checking. Ever since that county safety award, certain people have been going through my inspection reports like they’re looking for something, and the budget questions are… pointed. Like they’re trying to make it look like I did something crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s routine review, and I’m trying to consider that, I really am, but I can’t shake the sense that it’s coordinated to discredit me.
Do you think these people at work would be investigating you if you hadn't received the county safety award?

Honestly, no… I don’t think they would be looking this hard if I hadn’t gotten that award.

I mean, maybe reviews happen anyway, I understand that. I’m not trying to make it sound bigger than it is. But the timing is what bothers me. After the county safety award, certain people started going through my inspection reports differently, asking these budget questions like they were trying to catch me or make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s normal review, and I’m trying to be fair about that, but it really feels like the award put a target on me.
Do you think it's possible that you're misinterpreting your coworkers' actions and intentions?

I mean… I suppose it’s possible I’m reading too much into some of it. I don’t want to be unfair to anyone or sound like I’m accusing people without reason.

But from where I’m sitting, it really doesn’t feel like a misunderstanding. Ever since that county safety award, certain people have been twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, and I’m trying to take that seriously, but… I can tell there’s something coordinated going on to discredit me.
Do you believe that people outside of your workplace are also involved in this effort to discredit you?

I… I don’t really want to drag other people into it if I’m not sure, you know? I’m trying to keep this fair.

What I know is mostly at work. Since the county safety award, certain people there have been twisting my inspection reports and asking those pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, and I’m trying to accept that if that’s what it is, but it still feels coordinated to discredit me.

As far as people outside the workplace… I haven’t really seen enough to say that.
Do you think your belief about being targeted at work could be wrong?

I guess… technically, yes, it could be wrong. I mean, I’m trying to stay open to what you’re saying, and I don’t want to come across like I’m refusing to consider it.

But honestly, it doesn’t feel wrong to me. I’m here because ever since I got that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, and I hear that, I do… but I can tell there’s something coordinated going on to discredit me. I know that probably sounds strong, but that’s how it feels from my side.
How long have you felt like you're being targeted at work?

It’s been… about a year, I think. Since I got recognized for that county safety initiative.

I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but that’s when I started noticing things feeling different at work. So, yeah—around a year.
Do you think your belief about being targeted at work is something that you might be able to change your mind about if you found out more information?

I mean… I’d like to think I could, if there was really clear information. I don’t want to be unreasonable about it.

But it’s hard, because from what I’ve seen, ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions, and it makes me look like I’m crooked or doing something wrong. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, and I’m trying to respect that, but… I can still tell there’s something coordinated there, like they’re trying to discredit me.

So, yes, I’d listen to more information. I just don’t know what would explain all of it away.
Do you think your belief about being targeted at work is based on facts that anyone else could verify?

I think… parts of it, yes. Like, the reports and the budget questions are real things. Someone could look at those and see what I’m talking about, I think.

Maybe the part where I say it’s coordinated is harder to prove, and I know that probably sounds like I’m jumping ahead. I don’t want to overstate it. But ever since that county safety award, it’s felt like certain people have been twisting my inspection reports and asking questions in a way that makes me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, and I hear that, but from my side it doesn’t feel random.

So… some facts are verifiable, yes. The intent behind it, I guess, is what people might argue with.
Has your belief that you're being targeted at work caused you significant distress or problems in your daily life or relationships?

I mean… I wouldn’t say it’s ruined everything or anything like that. I still go to work, I still do what I’m supposed to do.

But, yeah, it has made some things harder. The compliance reviews feel a lot more tense than they used to, and mentoring the newer inspectors… I guess I’m more guarded now. And I’ve pulled back from a few coworkers I used to trust, which I don’t feel great about.

I’m trying not to let it affect people around me too much, but it has changed how I act at work, if that makes sense.
Do you still believe that your coworkers are trying to discredit you, even when your supervisor tells you it's just a normal review?

Yeah… I mean, I’m trying to take what he says seriously. I don’t want to be difficult or act like I know better than everyone.

But honestly, yes, I still believe there’s something going on. Ever since that county safety award, it’s like certain people started twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions in a way that makes me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just a normal review, and maybe some of it is, but I can tell it’s not just random. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.
How long have you held the belief that your coworkers are trying to discredit you?

It’s been… about a year, I guess. Since I got recognized for that county safety initiative.

I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but that’s when I started noticing the shift. Around then is when it felt like people started looking at my reports differently. So, yeah… roughly a year.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't believe your coworkers were trying to discredit you since you started feeling that way?

Not really, no. I mean… I’ve tried to talk myself out of it, especially when my supervisor says it’s just a normal review. I don’t want to be the guy making a big issue out of regular workplace stuff.

But since that award, it’s kind of stayed with me. The way some people handle my inspection reports, the budget questions… it still feels like they’re trying to make me look crooked. I haven’t had a stretch where I fully believed it was nothing, if that’s what you mean.
Would finding out that your coworkers' actions were actually a result of a new company policy, rather than a personal attack on you, change your belief about being targeted at work?

I’d want to believe that, honestly. If there was real proof it was just a new company policy, I’d try to take that seriously.

But… I don’t know. The way it started after that county safety award, and the way certain people have been handling my inspection reports and asking those pointed budget questions… it still feels personal, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. Maybe that’s not the answer I’m supposed to give, but even with an explanation like that, I think I’d still wonder if the policy was being used to discredit me.
Do you think your belief about being targeted at work could be considered an unreasonable or unrealistic concern by others?

I mean… yeah, I can see how other people might hear it and think I’m overreacting, or that it sounds unrealistic. I don’t want to come across like I’m accusing everyone for no reason.

But from where I’m sitting, it doesn’t feel unreasonable. Ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been treating my inspection reports differently, asking these pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s normal review, and I’m trying to keep that in mind, but… it still feels coordinated to me. Like I can tell there’s an effort to discredit me.
Have you ever had a time, even briefly, where you didn't feel like you were being targeted at work since this all started?

I guess… not really. I mean, there are moments where I’m busy and I’m not thinking about it every second, so maybe it eases up a little.

But if I stop and look at what’s going on, it comes back to the same thing. Since that county safety award, certain people have been twisting my inspection reports and asking those budget questions in a way that feels pointed, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. Even when my supervisor says it’s just normal review, I still feel like there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me. I know that probably sounds like a lot, but that’s honestly how it feels.
Do you think there's any evidence that would completely convince you that you're not being targeted at work?

I’d like to say yes, because I know that probably sounds more reasonable.

Maybe if someone could show me everything was just standard procedure, and that everybody’s reports were being handled the same way… I’d try to accept that. I don’t want to be stubborn about it.

But honestly, I don’t know if it would completely convince me. Because from what I’ve seen since that county safety award, the way certain people have been twisting my inspection reports and asking those pointed budget questions, it feels like they’re trying to make me look crooked. Even when my supervisor says it’s normal review, I still feel like there’s something coordinated going on to discredit me. So… I guess I’d worry there was still something behind it, even if the explanation sounded good.
Do you think anyone else would agree that you're being targeted at work?

I think… maybe a couple people would at least understand why I’m worried, if they saw it the way I’m seeing it. I don’t know if they’d come right out and say I’m being targeted, and I don’t want to put words in anyone’s mouth.

My supervisor doesn’t agree, really — he keeps saying it’s just normal review. But since that county safety award, the way certain people have been twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions… it feels like they’re trying to make me look crooked. So I guess I think if someone looked closely enough, they’d see there’s something coordinated going on to discredit me. Does that make sense?
Do you think your belief that you're being targeted at work could change if you were to discover that the award you received was not as significant as you thought?

Maybe… I mean, I can see why you’re asking that. If the award wasn’t as big a deal as I thought, then maybe I’d have to rethink some of why it started then.

But I don’t know that it would change everything, honestly. Because the part that bothers me is what happened after — certain people twisting my inspection reports, and those budget questions being asked in a way that felt like they were trying to make me look crooked. Even when my supervisor says it’s just normal review, it still feels coordinated to me, like they’re trying to discredit me.

I’m not trying to sound unreasonable. I just… I don’t think the award being smaller would fully explain away what I’ve been seeing.
